newsitem.title: LATVIA: KAPITAL BANKA GETS LICENCE TO TAKE DEPOSITS.
newsitem.headline: KAPITAL BANKA GETS LICENCE TO TAKE DEPOSITS.

text.p: Kapital-Banka, Latvia's 11th largest bank in terms of assets, said on Wednesday it has received a licence from the central bank allowing it to accept deposits from individuals.
The bank said in a statement that it had received "a full operating licence, which permits the bank to accept current and term deposits from individuals".
Following the severe banking crisis which hit the country in 1995, the new law on credit institutions demanded this licence since early last year.
Two years of international audit and a minimum of one million lats of own capital are among the conditions.
Some 16 of Latvia's banks currently are full licence holders.
